_doc: Placement entries read from the position ledgers (history/positions/positions_{A,B,C,D,E}.jsonl: A to D the OR27 reports, E the state regimental volumes, history layer v8). Every entry names the ledger claim that supports it; `claims` holds a digest of each claim used (id, report, printed page, verified quote, tier, fidelity check, printed time and place) and of the claims it conflicts with. A phrase is in the claim's verified quote, in its printed place or road words, or in the cited OR record as confirmed by tools/verify_claim_phrases.py. Nothing here is a coordinate: places and roads are gazetteer entries.

rule.used_if: claim_support_verified true, fidelity_check passed_full_read or corrected, tier documented or inferred
rule.time: a printed clock (t_iso confirmed by the words of the claim) or a printed named period (night, evening, dusk) with the labelled convention of placement.mjs
rule.conflict: two claims of one unit at the same place at different hours within 90 minutes, or two roads of approach for one unit (or a road that differs from the PDF ledger row): neither is placed, both are listed; two different places are a march, judged by the reachability check
rule.tier: inferred for every entry (the claim is the OR27 report; the place or road is a repository gazetteer entry, which is inferred); the claim's own tier is claim_tier

approach.phrase: the road between Taneytown and Gettysburg
approach.identification: printed as the road between Taneytown and Gettysburg: the road named by its two ends, the gazetteer’s Taneytown Road (the ledger references GZ-042, “by inference” from those words); the two ends are the words of the claim, the name is the gazetteer’s
approach.note: Dispatch of Meade’s chief of staff to the Sixth Corps, 1 July, no hour printed (OR27-3-D0967, printed p. 462): “the Second Corps is on the road between Taneytown and Gettysburg”. A position statement that puts the corps on its road to the field before it came on (it reached the field early on 2 July). The other document of the same day (the circular, POS-B-us-2c-19: the corps “now at Taneytown”) differs in place, not in road, and is listed on the card as a conflict. The statement sits inside a sentence about a possible fight (the ledger’s fidelity note); the corps’ position on the road is stated as a fact.
approach.inference: the claim is a position statement: its printed words put the formation on the road before it reached the field, and it is read as the road of its approach (DEC-013 a; DEC-014; approach tier inferred)

PD-1c-mclaws-semmes-05.activity: Semmes' brigade came by the Chambersburg-Gettysburg road with McLaws' division on July 1.

PD-1c-mclaws-wofford-04.author: Lieut. Gen. James Longstreet

place.direction_or_road: [inferred] Kershaw prints 'the Gettysburg road' from Fayetteville for his brigade; Longstreet names no road for the division's march

PD-1c-mclaws-wofford-04.activity: Wofford's brigade came by the Chambersburg-Gettysburg road with McLaws' division on July 1.

PD-2c-03.author: Lieut. Gen. Richard S. Ewell
PD-2c-03.quote: Next morning, I moved with Rodes' division toward Cashtown, ordering Early to follow by

place.direction_or_road: the Middletown road (Rodes); the Heidlersburg road (Early)

PD-2c-03.activity: On July 1 Ewell moved with Rodes' division toward Cashtown, ordering Early to follow by Hunterstown; before reaching Middletown he received notice from Hill that he was advancing on Gettysburg, turned the head of Rodes' column toward Gettysburg by the Middletown road and sent word to Early to advance directly on the Heidlersburg road.

PD-2c-early-02.author: Gen. Robert E. Lee
PD-2c-early-02.quote: Early, coming up by the Heidlei-sburg road soon afterward, took position on the left
PD-2c-early-02.activity: Lee: Early, coming up by the Heidlersburg road soon after Rodes arrived, took position on the left of Rodes, when a general advance was made.

PD-2c-early-06.author: Maj. Gen. Jubal A. Early
PD-2c-early-06.quote: I determined next morning (July 1) to march by the way of Heidlersburg, and

place.direction_or_road: the direct road from Heidlersburg to Gettysburg (as printed); 'turnpike' and 'north-east' were the compiler's additions and are removed

PD-2c-early-06.activity: Because the road to Hunterstown was rough and circuitous Early marched by Heidlersburg, then received Ewell's note that Hill was moving from Cashtown toward Gettysburg and Rodes had turned off at Middletown, and continued on the direct road from Heidlersburg to Gettysburg.

PD-2c-early-07.author: Maj. Gen. Jubal A. Early
PD-2c-early-07.quote: formed my line across the Heidlersburg road, with Gordon's brigade on the right, Hoke's
PD-2c-early-07.activity: Division formed across the Heidlersburg road: Gordon right, Hoke (Avery) left, Hays center, Smith behind Hoke; Jones' battalion on the left of the road in front of Hoke fired on the enemy flank; Gordon then ordered to Doles' support, Hays and Hoke forward.

PD-2c-early-gordon-02.author: Brig. Gen. J. B. Gordon
PD-2c-early-gordon-02.quote: About 3 p. m. I was ordered to move my Indgade forward to the

place.printed: to the supp(jrt of Major-General Rodes' left

PD-2c-early-gordon-02.activity: About 3 p. m. Gordon was ordered to move forward in support of Rodes' left; advanced slowly, charged the line on the crest (Barlow's division), driving it back and capturing Barlow; the 26th Georgia was detached to support the artillery under Lt. Col. Jones.

PD-2c-early-gordon-04.author: Maj. Gen. Jubal A. Early
PD-2c-early-gordon-04.quote: formed my line across the Heidlersburg road, with Gordon's brigade on the right
PD-2c-early-gordon-04.activity: Early's division formed across the Heidlersburg road on July 1 with Gordon's brigade on the right, Hoke's on the left, Hays' in the center and Smith's in the rear of Hoke's; Gordon's brigade was then ordered forward to the support of Doles' brigade on Rodes' left.

PD-2c-early-hays-01.author: Brig. Gen. Harry T. Hays
PD-2c-early-hays-01.quote: arrived with my brigade on the Heidlersburg road, within a mile and a half
PD-2c-early-hays-01.activity: After a march of 13 or 14 miles returning from York, Hays' brigade arrived on the Heidlersburg road within 1 1/2 miles of Gettysburg and found a space in the division line left for it; formed across the road, Fifth, Sixth and right wing of the Ninth on the right of the road, left wing of the Ninth, Seventh and Eighth on the left.

PD-2c-early-hays-02.author: Brig. Gen. Harry T. Hays
PD-2c-early-hays-02.quote: Brigadier-General Gordon, a little after 2 o'clock, was ordered to advance
PD-2c-early-hays-02.activity: A little after 2 o'clock Gordon was ordered to advance; Hays advanced in support when Gordon met the enemy in force, Hoke moving forward on his left; reached the railroad, changed front forward on the first company of the Fifth to meet a column on his right, then advanced through the city; line rested on one of the upper southern streets with Hoke on the left until 12 o'clock that night.

PD-2c-early-hoke-01.author: Col. Archibald C. Godwin
PD-2c-early-hoke-01.quote: On July 1, we advanced upon Gettysburg, along the Heidler.sLurg road, and, when distant

place.printed: on the left of the road

PD-2c-early-hoke-01.activity: Hoke's brigade (Sixth, Twenty-first and Fifty-seventh regiments; the 54th NC away at Staunton) advanced along the Heidlersburg road and formed on the left of the road 1 1/2 miles from town with its right on Hays; at 3 p. m. the order to advance was received; crossed a slough about 200 yards from the enemy and took the fence; two Napoleons taken by the Sixth; wheeled left on the railroad.

PD-2c-early-jones-05.author: Col. J. Thompson Brown
PD-2c-early-jones-05.quote: Lieutenant-Colonel Jones' battalion, coming up on the York road with Early's division
PD-2c-early-jones-05.activity: Brown (chief of artillery, II Corps): on July 1 Lieutenant-Colonel Jones' battalion, coming up on the York road with Early's division, also engaged the enemy, advancing upon Rodes' left and Early's right, and with fine effect (after Carter's battalion had engaged with Rodes' division).

PD-2c-early-smith-04.author: Maj. Gen. Jubal A. Early
PD-2c-early-smith-04.quote: Smith's brigade in the rear of Hoke's
PD-2c-early-smith-04.activity: Smith's brigade formed in the rear of Hoke's on the Heidlersburg road in Early's July 1 line; later in Early's report (a different part of the same report) Early had sent an order to Smith to advance, which Smith did not obey on account of a report that the enemy was advancing on the York road, and Smith's message of a large force advancing on the York road led Early to send Gordon to take charge of Smith's brigade as well and to keep a lookout on that road.

PD-2c-johnson-02.author: Gen. Robert E. Lee
PD-2c-johnson-02.quote: trains of his corps, and consequently did not reach Gettysburg until a late hour

place.direction_or_road: the road west of the mountains (the passage's words; the intermediate towns named earlier were the compiler's)

PD-2c-johnson-02.activity: Lee: Johnson's division, marching from Carlisle by the road west of the mountains to guard the corps trains, did not reach Gettysburg until a late hour on July 1.

PD-2c-johnson-03.author: Lieut. Gen. James Longstreet
PD-2c-johnson-03.quote: by Johnson's division, of the Second Corps, which came into the road from Shippensburg

place.direction_or_road: [compiler gloss, not printed] the Chambersburg-Gettysburg road; the passage says only 'the road' into which Johnson's division came from Shippensburg

PD-2c-johnson-03.activity: Longstreet: Johnson's division of the Second Corps came into the road from Shippensburg on July 1 with the long wagon trains that followed it and greatly delayed the First Corps march.

PD-2c-johnson-07.author: Maj. Gen. Edward Johnson
PD-2c-johnson-07.quote: Late on the night of July 1, I moved along the Gettysburg and York

when.printed: Late on the night of July 1

PD-2c-johnson-07.activity: Johnson moved late on the night of July 1 along the Gettysburg and York Railroad to the northeast of the town and formed line in a ravine in an open field: Nicholls on the right next Jones; Steuart and Walker on the left; pickets out; slept on their arms.

PD-2c-johnson-andrews-01.author: Lieut. Col. R. Snowden Andrews
PD-2c-johnson-andrews-01.quote: Major Latimer moved the battalion from its camp near Chambersburg on July 1, and,
PD-2c-johnson-andrews-01.activity: Andrews' battalion (Major Latimer commanding) left camp near Chambersburg on July 1, moved by the Chambersburg road, appeared in front of Gettysburg just before dark, and after dark by a detour moved to the extreme left between the York and Baltimore roads facing Cemetery Hill and parked for the night.

PD-2c-johnson-jones-01.author: Brig. Gen. J. M. Jones
PD-2c-johnson-jones-01.quote: July 1, the second brigade in the division column, and on reaching Gettysburg, late

place.direction_or_road: the road to Gettysburg; the railroad depot

PD-2c-johnson-jones-01.activity: Jones' brigade left camp at 7 a. m. July 1 as the second brigade in the division column, reached Gettysburg late in the afternoon, passed by the railroad depot to the left of the town and formed about dark on the left of Nicholls' brigade in a ravine in an open field northeast of the town; pickets out; lay on their arms.

PD-2c-johnson-jones-42va-01.author: Capt. Jesse M. Richardson
PD-2c-johnson-jones-42va-01.quote: It left camp near Scotland, Pa., on the morning of July 1, and arrived

place.direction_or_road: the road from Scotland to Gettysburg

PD-2c-johnson-jones-42va-01.activity: 42nd Virginia left camp near Scotland, Pa., on the morning of July 1, arrived at Gettysburg about sunset and was placed near the extreme left of the lines; about "4" o'clock (OCR) July 2 followed the 25th toward the enemy to support the division batteries, halted at the stone house two hours, then formed between the 50th and 48th and advanced into the woods; held position about 50 yards from the creek through the night and next day; moved on the morning of the 4th.

PD-2c-johnson-jones-44va-01.author: Capt. T. R. Buckner
PD-2c-johnson-jones-44va-01.quote: regiment reached the scene of action about sunset, July 1, and lay in line
PD-2c-johnson-jones-44va-01.activity: 44th Virginia reached the scene about sunset July 1, lay in line that night and the next day till about 3 p. m. (furious shelling), the advance began about 6 o'clock (OCR "0"), crossed the creek and charged up the hill; fell back to ledge of rocks about 150 yards from the works; skirmished July 3; fell back about 2 o'clock on the morning of July 4.

PD-2c-johnson-nicholls-01.author: Col. J. M. Williams
PD-2c-johnson-nicholls-01.quote: On July 1, at about 7 o'clock, while marching on the Cashtown road and

place.direction_or_road: Cashtown road, then along the railroad east of Gettysburg

PD-2c-johnson-nicholls-01.activity: Nicholls' brigade (Colonel J. M. Williams), in front of the division on the Cashtown road, was ordered about 7 o'clock July 1 to move to the east of Gettysburg along the railroad about 3/4 mile from town and formed line on the extreme right of the division 600 yards from the railroad; remained there until 7 p. m. July 2.

PD-2c-johnson-steuart-01.author: Brig. Gen. George H. Steuart
PD-2c-johnson-steuart-01.quote: reached the battle-field of July 1 toward evening of that day, and, marching through
PD-2c-johnson-steuart-01.activity: Steuart's brigade reached the field toward evening of July 1, marched through a part of the town and along the York railroad and formed line of battle to the northeast, facing south.

PD-2c-johnson-stonewall-01.author: Brig. Gen. James A. Walker
PD-2c-johnson-stonewall-01.quote: the evening of July 1, the brigade, with the rest of the division, arrived
PD-2c-johnson-stonewall-01.activity: Stonewall Brigade arrived at Gettysburg on the evening of July 1 and after nightfall took position on the southeast side of the town near the Hanover road, on the extreme left of the line, on Culp's farm, with skirmishers out.

PD-2c-johnson-stonewall-27va-01.author: Lieut. Col. Daniel M. Shriver
PD-2c-johnson-stonewall-27va-01.quote: Pa. , to Gettysburg, at which latter place we arrived a little before dark
PD-2c-johnson-stonewall-27va-01.activity: 27th Virginia marched from Fayetteville to Gettysburg, arriving a little before dark July 1, and lay about 2 miles to the left of Gettysburg that night; about 5 p. m. July 2 moved by the right flank to a line 300 yards in advance; at daybreak July 3 occupied the hill in front of the enemy's fortifications; withdrew about 10 p. m. July 4.

PD-2c-johnson-stonewall-33va-01.author: Capt. J. B. GoUaday
PD-2c-johnson-stonewall-33va-01.quote: Leaving bivouac near Chambersburg, the regiment reached Gettysburg late on the evening of the
PD-2c-johnson-stonewall-33va-01.activity: 33rd Virginia left a bivouac near Chambersburg and reached Gettysburg late on the evening of July 1, halted several hours on the July 1 battlefield and some time in the night took position on the extreme left; July 3 engaged the enemy intrenched on the hill for about five hours; fell back after nightfall.

PD-2c-johnson-stonewall-5va-01.author: Col. J. H. S. Funk
PD-2c-johnson-stonewall-5va-01.quote: regiment left camp near Fayetteville with the brigade

place.direction_or_road: [compiler gloss, not printed] the Chambersburg-Gettysburg pike; Funk says only that the regiment 'crossed South Mountain, and marched in the direction of Gettysburg' and followed 'the York and Gettysburg Railroad'

PD-2c-johnson-stonewall-5va-01.activity: 5th Virginia left camp near Fayetteville on the morning of July 1, crossed South Mountain, reached Gettysburg near dark, passed through a portion of the town and followed the York and Gettysburg railroad nearly 2 miles, then filed right into line northeast of the town, on the extreme left of the division.

PD-2c-rodes-02.author: Gen. Robert E. Lee
PD-2c-rodes-02.quote: About 2.30 p. m. the advance of Ewell's corps
PD-2c-rodes-02.activity: Lee: about 2.30 p. m. the advance of Ewell's corps, Rodes' division with Carter's battalion, arrived by the Middletown road, formed on Heth's left nearly at right angles to his line and became warmly engaged.

PD-2c-rodes-04.author: Maj. Gen. R. E. Rodes
PD-2c-rodes-04.quote: upon arriving at Middletown, and hearing that Lieutenant-General Hill's corps was moving upon Gettysburg,

place.direction_or_road: Middletown road (Ewell and Lee name it the Middletown road)

PD-2c-rodes-04.activity: On July 1 at Middletown, hearing that Hill was moving on Gettysburg, the head of Rodes' column was turned toward Gettysburg by order of Ewell; within 4 miles of the town a sharp cannonade was heard; the division moved along the summit of the wooded ridge with Doles on the left, O'Neal in the center and Iverson on the right, then by the right flank to a prominent hill from which Carter's battalion opened.

PD-2c-rodes-carter-01.author: Lieut. Col. Thomas H. Carter
PD-2c-rodes-carter-01.quote: field, July 1, the enemy was found to be in possession of a high
PD-2c-rodes-carter-01.activity: Carter's battalion (batteries of W. P. Carter, Page, Fry and Reese) reached the field July 1 when Hill was engaged; Carter's and Fry's batteries were ordered to a high point in front of Rodes' lines, near the Cashtown turnpike, and enfiladed the enemy's lines; Rodes then sent for two batteries (Page and Reese), and Page opened from the foot of the high ridge on the infantry advancing on O'Neal; on Doles' request, Carter's, Page's and Reese's batteries were put at the foot of the high ridge in rear of Doles' brigade; the battalion followed the advance, a few pieces unlimbering from time to time.

PD-2c-rodes-carter-03.author: Gen. Robert E. Lee
PD-2c-rodes-carter-03.quote: About 2.30 p. m. the advance of Ewell's corps, consisting of Rodes" division,
PD-2c-rodes-carter-03.activity: Lee: about 2.30 p. m. the advance of Ewell's corps, Rodes' division with Carter's battalion of artillery, arrived by the Middletown road, formed on Heth's left nearly at right angles to his line and became warmly engaged.

PD-2c-rodes-daniel-01.author: Brig. Gen. Junius Daniel
PD-2c-rodes-daniel-01.quote: we marched upon Gettysburg, by way of Heidlersburg, and arrived within 2^ miles of

place.direction_or_road: the road by way of Heidlersburg

PD-2c-rodes-daniel-01.activity: Daniel's brigade marched from Carlisle June 30 by way of Heidlersburg and on July 1 arrived within 2 1/2 miles of Gettysburg about 12 m., turned to the right, followed the troops that had preceded it, and formed in line about 200 yards in rear of Iverson to protect the division's right; after an hour and a half Iverson advanced; Daniel engaged near a railroad cut and a stone barn, and by his own later statement entered the fight about 1 p. m. and was engaged until 4 p. m.

PD-2c-rodes-daniel-2ncbn-01.author: Capt. Van Brown
PD-2c-rodes-daniel-2ncbn-01.quote: The original position in line of the battalion was on the left of the
PD-2c-rodes-daniel-2ncbn-01.activity: 2nd NC Battalion on the left of the brigade; the 43rd and 53rd shifted left putting it in the center; moved forward nearly 1 1/2 miles through open fields, encountered the enemy near the railroad cut and ridge behind it; Lt. Col. Andrews killed in the final charge; rested night of July 1 under a railroad embankment; July 2 between the 32nd and 53rd; July 3 on the right of the brigade as skirmishers.

PD-2c-rodes-daniel-32nc-01.author: Col. E. C. Brabble
PD-2c-rodes-daniel-32nc-01.quote: on the right of the brigade, and, advancing, met, the enemy about 4 o'clock

when.printed: On the first day, about 2.30 p. m.

PD-2c-rodes-daniel-32nc-01.activity: 32nd NC drawn up about 2.30 p. m. on the brigade's right, met the enemy about 4 o'clock near the railroad cut and barn, took the barn, advanced to the edge of the town; July 2 posted behind the theological seminary as support to batteries; July 3 moved with the brigade to the left and front northeast of Gettysburg, advanced to the foot of the hill, then formed on the right of the 43rd to hold a captured entrenchment; fell back about 5 p. m. and withdrew a little before midnight to the range of hills west of Gettysburg.

PD-2c-rodes-daniel-43nc-01.author: Lieut. Col. "W. G. Lewis
PD-2c-rodes-daniel-43nc-01.quote: 1 o'clock, July 1, we were drawn up in line of battle, about 2
PD-2c-rodes-daniel-43nc-01.activity: 43rd NC drawn up about 1 o'clock July 1 about 2-2 1/2 miles from Gettysburg, advanced about a mile to a lane, was shifted left to support the 2nd NC Battalion and 45th NC, advanced to the railroad cut, rested behind the railroad embankment; July 2 on the crest of the hill held by the enemy on July 1; about 4 o'clock the batteries opened; July 3 at about sunrise entered the action on the mountain side.

PD-2c-rodes-daniel-53nc-01.author: Col. WUliam A. Owens
PD-2c-rodes-daniel-53nc-01.quote: and was in line of battle at or about 1 o'clock
PD-2c-rodes-daniel-53nc-01.activity: 53rd NC in line of battle at or about 1 o'clock July 1 within 2 miles of Gettysburg, moved to support Iverson, advanced through a wheat-field, joined the 12th NC through the woods to the railroad embankment and the edge of the town; July 2 behind the railroad embankment, then in rear of Lane's brigade; July 3 about 2-3 a. m. moved through Gettysburg around to the right of the enemy (the report says about 4 miles) to the foot of a hill with the 32nd NC on its right.

PD-2c-rodes-doles-01.author: Brig. Gen. George Doles
PD-2c-rodes-doles-01.quote: This brigade was formed into line of battle about 1 p. m. July 1,
PD-2c-rodes-doles-01.activity: Doles' brigade formed line of battle about 1 p. m. July 1 on the left of Rodes' division, drove the enemy's cavalry picket from a hill about 3.30 p. m.; moved by the left flank; with Gordon's brigade attacked the enemy behind a rock fence; routed a force on its right flank; moved by the left flank through the town as far as its outer edge; halted and formed in the street running east and west.

PD-2c-rodes-doles-03.author: Maj. 'V\^ H. WilUs

place.direction_or_road: Heidlersburg to Gettysburg (Rodes names the Middletown road)

PD-2c-rodes-doles-03.activity: Doles' brigade, inferred from the 4th Georgia: on the morning of July 1, while on the march from Heidlersburg to Gettysburg, the regiment heard artillery firing in front, was brought by a quick march to the neighborhood of Gettysburg and was at once placed in line of battle ('say at 13 o'clock', OCR-damaged hour); the brigade is taken to have marched with the regiment.

PD-2c-rodes-doles-21ga-01.author: Col. John T. Mercer
PD-2c-rodes-doles-21ga-01.quote: On the evening of July 1, at about 4 o'clock. Doles' brigade was drawn
PD-2c-rodes-doles-21ga-01.activity: 21st Georgia: Doles' brigade drawn up about 4 o'clock July 1 on the north side of Gettysburg in the order 21st, 44th, 4th, 12th Georgia; the 21st wheeled right across a wheat-field to meet a flank force, advanced into the town, was ordered to hold the street from the court-house to the eastward; after dark July 2 advanced in line on the west side of town about half a mile, retired a quarter of a mile; on the morning of July 4 took position on the hill at the theological college.

PD-2c-rodes-doles-4ga-01.author: Maj. 'V\^ H. WilUs
PD-2c-rodes-doles-4ga-01.quote: the enemy making a demonstration in our front at the same time
PD-2c-rodes-doles-4ga-01.activity: 4th Georgia, marching from Heidlersburg on the morning of July 1, heard artillery, was placed in line (say at "13 o'clock", OCR) near Gettysburg, advanced, drove the enemy from the field and occupied the town; position changed to the south side of the town late on the 2d and to the heights about half a mile distant on the morning of the 4th.

PD-2c-rodes-iverson-01.author: Brig. Gen. Alfred Iverson
PD-2c-rodes-iverson-01.quote: my brigade, being in the advance of Maj. Gen. R. E. Rodes' division

place.printed: a wooded height overlooking the plain and the town

PD-2c-rodes-iverson-01.activity: Iverson's brigade, in the advance of Rodes' division, was ordered by Rodes to form line of battle and advance toward the firing at Gettysburg, crossed a wooded height overlooking the plain and the town, and was moved by Rodes by the right flank with a changed direction of the line; it supported the batteries during the cannonade, then advanced to within 100 yards of an enemy strongly posted in woods behind a concealed stone wall; the enemy charged and captured nearly all that were left unhurt in three regiments, and 500 of his men were left lying dead and wounded in a line.

PD-2c-rodes-iverson-04.author: Maj. Gen. R. E. Rodes

place.direction_or_road: Middletown road to the wooded ridge

PD-2c-rodes-iverson-04.activity: Iverson's brigade came with Rodes' division by way of Middletown (Rodes: 'the head of the column was turned' toward Gettysburg) along the wooded ridge on the left side of which Gettysburg is situated and took the right ('Iverson on the right') of the three-brigade line on July 1.

PD-2c-rodes-oneal-01.author: Col. E. A. O'Neal
PD-2c-rodes-oneal-01.quote: to move in the direction of Gettysburg, and arrived near the town July 1
PD-2c-rodes-oneal-01.activity: O'Neal (Rodes' old brigade) was ordered June 30 toward Gettysburg, arrived near the town July 1, formed to the right of the road in rear of the batteries, engaged under artillery fire more than an hour; the Sixth, Twelfth and Twenty-sixth Alabama advanced alone (Third with Daniel, Fifth held by Rodes), fought about half an hour and fell back; then charged with Ramseur's arrival and went through the town to the heights.

PD-2c-rodes-oneal-12al-01.author: Col. S. B. Pickens
PD-2c-rodes-oneal-12al-01.quote: We arrived near that place at 11 a. m. on July 1
PD-2c-rodes-oneal-12al-01.activity: 12th Alabama arrived near Gettysburg at 11 a. m. July 1, advanced about a mile in line of battle, stood an artillery duel of about an hour, then attacked and fell back after about fifteen minutes; half an hour later advanced with the whole division through the town; formed behind the railroad embankment; about 2 a. m. July 3 ordered to Johnson, arriving at daylight; attacked at 8 o'clock; withdrew at 12 o'clock that night; commenced falling back at 1 o'clock on the morning of the 5th.

PD-2c-rodes-oneal-26al-01.author: Lieut. Col. John C. Goodgame
PD-2c-rodes-oneal-26al-01.quote: at which place we engaged the enemy about 12 m. on July 1
PD-2c-rodes-oneal-26al-01.activity: 26th Alabama engaged the enemy about 12 m. July 1 near Gettysburg; not engaged on the 2d; on the morning of the 3d under Johnson's command, engaged at an early hour and unable to dislodge the enemy from his fortified position; at 2 a. m. July 4 retired and entrenched on a hill commanding the town; left the field at 12 p. m. toward Hagerstown.

PD-2c-rodes-oneal-5al-01.author: Col. J. M. Hall
PD-2c-rodes-oneal-5al-01.quote: regiment reached Gettysburg, Pa. , by way of Petersburg from Carlisle, Pa., July 1
PD-2c-rodes-oneal-5al-01.activity: 5th Alabama reached Gettysburg by way of Petersburg from Carlisle July 1, was in the movement of the brigade commencing about 2 miles from the town, moved 1 1/2 miles at a right wheel, was held in reserve within 500 yards of the enemy to protect Doles' right flank, then advanced; after the enemy was driven through the town was posted in rear of the railroad until late July 2, then forward and back to the street that continues the Cashtown road; sharpshooters under Major Blackford held the town July 3.

PD-2c-rodes-oneal-6al-01.author: Capt. M. L. Bowie
PD-2c-rodes-oneal-6al-01.quote: Heidlersburg toward Gettysburg, Pa., and, arriving in sight of the enemy's forces 3 miles
PD-2c-rodes-oneal-6al-01.activity: 6th Alabama marched from Heidlersburg toward Gettysburg on July 1 and, on coming in sight of the enemy 3 miles in advance of the town, was formed with Rodes' old brigade and engaged for a number of hours, aiding in driving the enemy through the town; July 2 not particularly engaged; July 3 in the charges on the enemy's right line of fortifications.

PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-01.author: Brig. Gen. S. D. Ramseur. C. S. Army
PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-01.quote: in rear of the division train, as a guard on the march from Heidlersburg
PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-01.activity: On July 1 Ramseur's brigade marched in rear of the division train from Heidlersburg to Gettysburg, guarding it, arrived after the division had formed line and was held in reserve; after about fifteen minutes the 2nd and 4th NC went to O'Neal and the 14th and 30th NC to Iverson; with the 3rd Alabama they turned the enemy's right at a wooded stone-fenced position, took 800-900 prisoners, pushed through Gettysburg to the heights beyond and formed in a street in Gettysburg running east and west.

PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-14nc-01.author: Maj. JIaj. J. H.. Lambeth. Fourteenth North Carolina Infantry
PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-14nc-01.quote: On July 1. about 2 p. m., the command was moved to the front,
PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-14nc-01.activity: 14th NC moved to the front about 2 p. m. July 1 after a forced march of 14 miles that morning, routed the enemy behind stone walls and drove them through town to the heights; stayed in town in line all night and until late July 2, then to the extreme right of the division connecting with Hill's left on an old road; on the morning of July 4 to a formidable position at the theological seminary; moved toward Hagerstown on the morning of the 5th.

PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-2nc-01.author: Capt. Orren Williams
PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-2nc-01.quote: went into action July 1, 1803, near the town of Gettysburg, Pa. , about
PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-2nc-01.activity: 2nd NC (Major Hurtt, wounded; Captain Scales then commanding) went into action about 1 p. m. July 1 near Gettysburg, maneuvered about half an hour, advanced through the field fronting the railroad under flank fire from a stone fence on its right, and followed the enemy into the town.

PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-30nc-01.author: Maj. W. W. Sniers
PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-30nc-01.quote: actively engaged only during the early part of the afternoon of Wednesday, July 1
PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-30nc-01.activity: 30th NC was actively engaged only during the early part of the afternoon of July 1, in the charge that drove the enemy from a stone wall on elevated ground into the plain in front of Gettysburg; Colonel Parker wounded; some losses among sharpshooters July 2-3.

PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-4nc-01.author: Col. Bryan Grimes
PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-4nc-01.quote: were under arms and on the march by sunrise. About 4 p. m.
PD-2c-rodes-ramseur-4nc-01.activity: 4th NC encamped near Heidlersburg on July 1, under arms and marching by sunrise, arrived near the battle-field about 4 p. m., with the 2nd NC was posted on a hill to cover an enemy advance, then advanced and was the first to enter Gettysburg; halted on the road to Fairfield; thursday dusk advanced for a night attack, recalled to the road; 3 a. m. Saturday (July 4) to the crest of the hill in the rear.

PD-3c-01.author: Lieut. Gen. Ambrose P. Hill
PD-3c-01.quote: morning of June 29, the Third Corps, composed of the divisions of Major-Generals Anderson,
PD-3c-01.activity: On June 29 the Third Corps was encamped on the Chambersburg-Gettysburg road near Fayetteville; Hill was directed to move toward York and cross the Susquehanna; on the 29th he moved Heth's division to Cashtown, some 8 miles from Gettysburg, on the 30th Pender's, and directed Anderson to follow on the morning of July 1.

PD-3c-02.author: Lieut. Gen. Ambrose P. Hill
PD-3c-02.quote: On July 1, at 5 a. m. , Heth took up the line of

place.direction_or_road: [compiler gloss, not printed] the Cashtown-Gettysburg turnpike; the passage says only that Heth 'took up the line of march' from Cashtown (the road is named in the next sentences as 'the road')

PD-3c-02.activity: July 1, 5 a. m.: Heth marched from Cashtown toward Gettysburg with Pegram's battalion, followed by Pender with McIntosh's battalion; Colonel Walker with the remaining artillery was with Anderson; about 3 miles from Gettysburg Archer's advance brigade met the enemy.

PD-3c-anderson-01.author: Maj. Gen. Richard H. Anderson
PD-3c-anderson-01.quote: in the direction of Cashtown. Arrived at the latter place early in the afternoon

place.direction_or_road: [compiler gloss, not printed] the Chambersburg-Gettysburg turnpike; the passage says only 'from Fayetteville in the direction of Cashtown' and 'to Gettysburg'

PD-3c-anderson-01.activity: Anderson's division left Fayetteville soon after daylight July 1, reached Cashtown early in the afternoon, heard cannonading, waited about an hour, was ordered forward and on approaching Gettysburg occupied the line vacated by Pender; Wilcox's brigade with Ross' battery was posted a mile or more to the right, facing right.

PD-3c-anderson-cutts-02.author: Maj. John Lane
PD-3c-anderson-cutts-02.quote: near wliich place we arrived about :i o'clock on the eveiung of the Jst

place.direction_or_road: the division's march through the Shenandoah Valley, across the Potomac, through Maryland and as far as Gettysburg

PD-3c-anderson-cutts-02.activity: Major Lane (Sumter Artillery Battalion) reported to Anderson on leaving Fredericksburg June 14 and accompanied his division through the Shenandoah Valley, across the Potomac and through Maryland as far as Gettysburg, near which place the command arrived about ':i' o'clock (OCR glyph; read as 3) on the evening of the 1st.

PD-3c-anderson-mahone-02.author: Brig. Gen. A. R. Wright
PD-3c-anderson-mahone-02.quote: my brigade was immediately in rear of Mahone's brigade

place.direction_or_road: the turnpike through Cashtown Gap toward Gettysburg (as printed: 'the turnpike', 'Cashtown Gap'); the compiler's 'Chambersburg-Gettysburg' is not printed

PD-3c-anderson-mahone-02.activity: Wright (R539): on the morning of July 1 his brigade moved from its camp near Fayetteville in the direction of Gettysburg, passing through the South Mountain at Cashtown Gap immediately in rear of Mahone's brigade; about 10 a. m., when within about 1 mile of Cashtown, it was stopped by the halt of Mahone's brigade in the road in its immediate front; after an hour or an hour and a half the column moved on, and Wright was directed to bivouac in timber to the right of the turnpike in rear of Mahone, who had preceded him into the woods.

PD-3c-anderson-perry-01.author: Col. David Lang
PD-3c-anderson-perry-01.quote: march from Fayetteville to Gettysburg, this brigade being the rear guard of Anderson's division,
PD-3c-anderson-perry-01.activity: Perry's brigade (Lang): on July 1, on the march from Fayetteville to Gettysburg as the rear guard of Anderson's division, heavy firing was heard in front; Lang was ordered by Anderson to pass ahead of the wagon train and close up on Wilcox's brigade and, within 2 miles of Gettysburg, to form line of battle about 1 mile to the right of the turnpike; on the morning of the 2d the division moved to the front and right about 'H' (OCR fraction; probably 1 1/2) miles and formed line behind an open field 1 mile wide; at 6 p. m. it moved forward when Wilcox advanced; after the repulse it reformed on the line from which it started.

PD-3c-anderson-posey-02.author: Maj. Gen. Richard H. Anderson
PD-3c-anderson-posey-02.quote: the division moved from Fayetteville in the direction of Cashtown

place.direction_or_road: [compiler gloss, not printed] the Chambersburg-Gettysburg turnpike; Anderson's passage says only 'in the direction of Cashtown'

PD-3c-anderson-posey-02.activity: Posey's brigade came with Anderson's division from Fayetteville through Cashtown toward Gettysburg on July 1; its own report begins on the morning of July 2 in an open field in rear of Pegram's battery.

PD-3c-anderson-wilcox-01.author: Brig. Gen
PD-3c-anderson-wilcox-01.quote: At 2.30 p. m. came within sight and hearing of a distant
PD-3c-anderson-wilcox-01.activity: Wilcox's brigade, after three days at Fayetteville, moved forward on the Chambersburg and Gettysburg turnpike on the morning of July 1; at 2.30 p. m. the division came within sight and hearing of a distant artillery fire; it filed off to the right of the road and halted an hour in the woods; resuming the march toward Gettysburg about '1+' (OCR; the fraction is unreadable) miles, the brigade filed off perpendicularly to the right of the road and marched nearly 1 mile, was joined by a battery, and remained on picket for the night beyond and to the rear, at right angles to the right flank of the rest of the division.

PD-3c-anderson-wright-01.author: Brig. Gen. A. R. Wright
PD-3c-anderson-wright-01.quote: Mahone's command. About 10 a. m., and when within about 1 mile of Cashtown
PD-3c-anderson-wright-01.activity: Wright's brigade followed Mahone's through Cashtown Gap on the morning of July 1; about 10 a. m., within about 1 mile of Cashtown, it was stopped by the halt of Mahone's brigade; artillery was heard seemingly not more than 'G or 8' miles distant (OCR; read as 6 or 8); after an hour or an hour and a half it moved to Cashtown and bivouacked in timber; about 1 p. m. it took the turnpike toward Gettysburg; Wright, ill, left; between 4 and 5 p. m. (per Colonel Gibson) the brigade reached a position three-fourths of a mile to the right of the turnpike and about '2^ or 3' miles (OCR fraction, probably 2 1/2) from Gettysburg and lay in line until next morning.

PD-3c-heth-01.author: Maj. Gen. Henry Heth
PD-3c-heth-01.quote: my division, accompanied by Pegrani's battalion of artillery, was ordered to move at 5
PD-3c-heth-01.activity: Heth's division left Cashtown at 5 a. m. July 1 with Pegram's battalion; at 9 o'clock Heth was still ignorant of the enemy's strength; on the summit of the second ridge west of Gettysburg a few shots from Marye's battery scattered the vedettes (mortally wounding Reynolds); the division within a mile of Gettysburg deployed Archer on the right and Davis on the left of the turnpike, Pettigrew and Brockenbrough in reserve.

PD-3c-heth-archer-01.author: Lieut. Col. S. G. Shepard
PD-3c-heth-archer-01.quote: We left our cam]) near Cashtown. Pa., early on the morning of July 1,

when.printed: early on the morning of July 1

PD-3c-heth-archer-01.activity: Archer's brigade (Shepard's report) left camp near Cashtown early on the morning of July 1 and marched down the turnpike road leading to Gettysburg; after about ':)' (OCR; read as 3) miles it came upon the enemy's pickets, who fell back before it for about '8' (OCR; probably 3) miles, to a slight eminence in front and to the right of the road; Archer halted while a section of a battery opened fire, then deployed and advanced through an open field to a creek and fence, was flanked from the right and forced back with about 75 men lost, Archer included; Colonel Fry then took command and the brigade advanced on the extreme right of the line in the afternoon.

PD-3c-heth-davis-03.author: Brig. Gen. Joseph R. Davis
PD-3c-heth-davis-03.quote: Early on the morning of the 1st, I moved in rear of Archer's brigade

when.printed: Early on the morning of the 1st

place.direction_or_road: a turnpike road leading to Gettysburg (as printed, 'turninke road'); 'Cashtown road' was the compiler's phrase

PD-3c-heth-davis-03.activity: Davis' brigade left the camp near Cashtown early July 1 in rear of Archer's by the turnpike leading to Gettysburg (three regiments; the 11th Mississippi stayed with the division train); within about 2 miles of town the artillery opened and Davis took position left of the turnpike.

PD-3c-heth-pettigrew-01.author: Maj. J. Jones
PD-3c-heth-pettigrew-01.quote: ultimo, the brigade was on picket on the
PD-3c-heth-pettigrew-01.activity: Pettigrew's brigade (Jones' report) picketed the turnpike road from Chambersburg to Gettysburg, about half way between Cashtown and Gettysburg, on the night of June 30; early on July 1 it moved down the pike toward Gettysburg, deployed when within about '2h' (OCR; probably 2 1/2) miles of the town to the left of the pike, crossed over to the right and stood in rear of the batteries about half an hour, then moved forward about half a mile and halted in a skirt of woods (52nd, 47th, 11th, 26th NC from right to left) and remained in line of battle until 2 p. m.

PD-3c-pender-01.author: Maj. Joseph A. Engelhard
PD-3c-pender-01.quote: on the north side of South Mountain, Pa., moved from that
PD-3c-pender-01.activity: Pender's (Light) division, encamped on the north side of South Mountain on the afternoon of June 30, moved at an hour damaged in the OCR ('S o"(dock'; the earlier reading was 8) on the morning of July 1 along the turnpike through Cashtown in the direction of Gettysburg in rear of Heth's division; within about 3 miles of Gettysburg it formed from right to left Perrin, Scales, Lane, Thomas (the first two on the right and the last two on the left of the turnpike), advanced nearly a mile and halted by Hill's order; about 3 o'clock, with Ewell's troops appearing on the left, Lane was ordered to the extreme right and Thomas to close on Scales' left, and a general advance was ordered, Thomas being retained by Hill against a threatened advance from the left; about 4 o'clock Pender ordered the three brigades to pass Heth and charge.

PD-3c-pender-lane-01.author: Brig. Gen. James H. Lane
PD-3c-pender-lane-01.quote: on the morning of July 1, we moved from South Mountain, Pa., through Cashtown
PD-3c-pender-lane-01.activity: Lane's brigade moved from South Mountain through Cashtown on the morning of July 1, formed line of battle about 3 miles from Gettysburg left of the turnpike in rear of Heth's left, advanced nearly a mile, and was moved to the extreme right of the Light division, where the 7th NC deployed as skirmishers to cover the right against enemy cavalry; the brigade then crossed the open field under fire from cavalry in the woods later occupied by Pegram's battalion and reached the stone fence in the peach orchard near McMillan's house; ordered by Pender not to advance farther.

PD-3c-pender-mcgowan-01.author: Col. Abner Perrin
PD-3c-pender-mcgowan-01.quote: About s o'clock on the morning of July 1, I received orders to get

place.direction_or_road: the turnpike leading to Gettysburg (as printed)

PD-3c-pender-mcgowan-01.activity: McGowan's brigade (Perrin commanding): about 's' o'clock (OCR glyph only; the earlier reading was 8) on the morning of July 1 Perrin received orders to get under arms, and the brigade, except Captain Hadden's Rifles left to guard the wagon train, commenced the march on the turnpike leading to Gettysburg at the head of the division, just in rear of Heth's division; within 3 miles of Gettysburg it was ordered to file down a road and form line of battle, leaving room for Scales' brigade between its left and the Gettysburg road, with skirmishers covering the right flank; it advanced through an open field about a mile and halted in support of Heth.

PD-3c-res-art-mcintosh-01.author: Maj. D. G. Mcintosh
PD-3c-res-art-mcintosh-01.quote: section of Whitworths were placed first in position a short distance to tlie right
PD-3c-res-art-mcintosh-01.activity: McIntosh's battalion moved with Pender's division into line July 1: Rice's battery and a Whitworth section right of the turnpike beside Pegram's battalion; Johnson's battery and the other Hurt section on a hill some distance to the right near the Fairfield road; Wallace's near the Cashtown pike; July 2 behind a stone wall on the range of hills left of Gettysburg; July 3 the two Whitworths north of the railroad cut by Hill's direction.

PD-3c-res-art-pegram-01.author: Capt. E. B. Brunson
PD-3c-res-art-pegram-01.quote: forward on the Baltimore pike, in rear of General Heth
PD-3c-res-art-pegram-01.activity: Pegram's battalion (Captain Brunson commanding in the report) moved July 1 in rear of Heth's division, Marye's section opened within 2 miles of Gettysburg, the battalion took a commanding position right and left of the pike a mile from town and engaged ten Napoleons and seven rifles against the Union batteries; Brander's battery reported to Davis; bivouacked there; early July 2 took a position a mile to the right of the pike; about 12 o'clock on the third day ordered to open and then to advance to the crest.

POS-A-11A-013.author: Maj. Gen. OUver O. Howard
POS-A-11A-013.quote: the head of column of the Eleventh Corps entered and passed through the town

place.printed: the town of Gettysburg, moving forward toward the position ordered

POS-A-11A-013.activity: About this time (about 12.30 p. m., the time given two sentences earlier) the head of column of the Eleventh Corps entered and passed through the town

POS-A-11A-016.author: Maj. Gen. OUver O. Howard
POS-A-11A-016.quote: At 4.10 p. m., finding that I could hold out no longer

place.printed: Cemetery Hill, Eleventh Corps right and First Corps left of the Baltimore pike

POS-A-11A-016.activity: At 4.10 p. m. Howard sent a positive order to the First and Eleventh Corps to fall back gradually to the position near the cemetery, Eleventh Corps on the right and First Corps on the left of the Baltimore pike

POS-A-11A-017.author: Maj. Gen. OUver O. Howard
POS-A-11A-017.quote: At 4.30 p. m. the columns reached Cemetery Hill
POS-A-11A-017.activity: At 4.30 p. m. the columns reached Cemetery Hill with the enemy pressing hard; Wiedrich's battery broke a single attempt to turn the right

POS-A-11A-022.author: Maj. Gen. OUver O. Howard
POS-A-11A-022.quote: At about 1 p. m. a terrific cannonade opened upon us from the west
POS-A-11A-022.activity: About 1 p. m. July 3 a terrific cannonade opened on the cemetery from the west, northwest, north and northeast

POS-A-11A-032.author: Col. Andrew L. Harris
POS-A-11A-032.quote: Arrived at Gettysburg at about 1 p. m.

place.printed: the northwest part of the city

POS-A-11A-032.activity: 75th Ohio arrived at Gettysburg at about 1 p. m. and was sent immediately to the northwest part of the city and placed in line of battle

POS-A-11A-036.author: Maj. Allen G. Brady
POS-A-11A-036.quote: arrived in Gettysburg between 1 and 2 p. m. of the 1st instant

place.printed: the lower end of the town

POS-A-11A-036.activity: 17th Connecticut arrived in Gettysburg between 1 and 2 p. m. on July 1 and was marched through to the lower end of the town

POS-A-11A-043.author: Lieut. Israel White
POS-A-11A-043.quote: placed in line of battle on the heights in the rear of Gettysburg

place.printed: the heights in the rear of Gettysburg

POS-A-11A-043.activity: On the evening of July 1 the regiment was placed in line of battle on the heights in the rear of Gettysburg and stayed until 2 p. m. of July 2, then relieved and took a position about 100 rods in the rear

POS-A-11A-045.author: Capt. John M. Lutz
POS-A-11A-045.quote: The regiment arrived at Gettysburg, Pa., at about 1 p. m. July 1
POS-A-11A-045.activity: 107th Ohio arrived at Gettysburg at about 1 p. m. July 1; at about 3 p. m. marched through the town to the front and engaged the enemy about half a mile north of the town until about 4 p. m.

POS-A-11A-048.author: Lieut. Col. Detleo von Einsiedel
POS-A-11A-048.quote: about 10 o'clock in the evening of July 1, at the cemetery near Gettysburg

when.printed: at about 10 o'clock in the evening of July 1

place.printed: the cemetery near Gettysburg, behind a square stone fence about 1 mile from Gettysburg to the right of the road from Baltimore

POS-A-11A-048.activity: 41st New York, coming from Emmitsburg, arrived at about 10 o'clock in the evening of July 1 at the cemetery near Gettysburg and bivouacked behind a square stone fence about 1 mile from Gettysburg right of the Baltimore road

POS-A-11A-052.author: Lieut. Col. Detleo von Einsiedel
POS-A-11A-052.quote: between 12 m. and 1 p. m. under a very heavy fire of artillery
POS-A-11A-052.activity: Between 12 m. and 1 p. m. July 3 the regiment stood under a very heavy artillery fire

POS-A-11B-008.author: Brig. Gen. Adolph von Steinwehr
POS-A-11B-008.quote: At about 4 p. m. the enemy's batteries opened a heavy fire
POS-A-11B-008.activity: At about 4 p. m. July 2 the enemy's batteries opened a heavy fire for two hours on Cemetery Hill from nine batteries

POS-A-11B-010.author: Brig. Gen. Adolph von Steinwehr
POS-A-11B-010.quote: At 2.30 o'clock the enemy again opened a terrific artillery fire
POS-A-11B-010.activity: At 2.30 o'clock July 3 the enemy again opened a terrific artillery fire on the hill, lasting until 4 p. m.

POS-A-11B-020.author: Maj. G«n. Carl Schurz
POS-A-11B-020.quote: at 7 a. m., the Third Division left its camp, near Saint Joseph's College

place.printed: its camp near Saint Joseph's College, Emmitsburg

POS-A-11B-020.activity: On July 1 at 7 a. m. the Third Division left its camp near St. Joseph's College at Emmitsburg with orders to march to Gettysburg by way of Horner's Mills

POS-A-11B-024.author: Maj. G«n. Carl Schurz
POS-A-11B-024.quote: arrived by the Emmitsburg road proper, advanced through the town

place.printed: the Emmitsburg road proper, through the town

POS-A-11B-024.activity: Shortly afterward the First Division under Barlow arrived by the Emmitsburg road proper, advanced through the town and formed on the right of the Third Division

POS-A-11B-030.author: Maj. G«n. Carl Schurz
POS-A-11B-030.quote: after 5 o'clock when the Eleventh Corps occupied the position on Cemetery Hill

place.printed: Cemetery Hill; the stone walls enclosing the cemetery on the west

POS-A-11B-030.activity: It was after 5 o'clock when the Eleventh Corps occupied the position on Cemetery Hill: Second Division behind the stone walls enclosing the cemetery on the west, Third Division opposite the town, First Division on the right

POS-A-11B-038.author: Lieut. Col. Adolphus Dobke
POS-A-11B-038.quote: where it arrived at 11 a. m.
POS-A-11B-038.activity: 45th New York marched early on July 1 from Emmitsburg to Gettysburg and arrived at 11 a. m., hurried at the double-quick to the right of the First Corps

POS-A-11B-042.author: Lieut. Col. Adolphus Dobke
POS-A-11B-042.quote: vehement artillery cross-fire had to be sustained from 12 m. to 4 p. m.
POS-A-11B-042.activity: The most vehement artillery cross-fire had to be sustained from 12 m. to 4 p. m. July 3, and particularly from 2 to 4 p. m.

POS-A-11B-043.author: Lieut. Col. William H. H. Bown
POS-A-11B-043.quote: and arrived at Gettysburg, Pa., at about 1.30 p. m.
POS-A-11B-043.activity: 61st Ohio marched from Emmitsburg at 9 a. m. and arrived at Gettysburg at about 1.30 p. m.; Bown states it was the advance regiment of the Third Division, ordered at the double-quick through the town and deployed as skirmishers

POS-A-11B-047.author: Capt. Emil Koenig
POS-A-11B-047.quote: we arrived at Gettysburg about 3.30 p. m.

place.printed: Gettysburg; a hill on the left of Cemetery Hill

POS-A-11B-047.activity: The detachment arrived at Gettysburg about 3.30 p. m., occupied a hill on the left of Cemetery Hill supporting a Second Corps battery, then reported to Schurz

POS-A-11B-051.author: Maj. Benjamin A. Willis
POS-A-11B-051.quote: about 12 o'clock that day, a distance of 11 miles
POS-A-11B-051.activity: 119th New York started for Gettysburg about 5 a. m. July 1 and reached there about 12 o'clock, 11 miles

POS-A-11B-061.author: Col. William H. Jacobs
POS-A-11B-061.quote: the regiment arrived with the rest of your command

place.printed: the village of Gettysburg; the extreme right of the brigade

POS-A-11B-061.activity: As stated to Colonel Jacobs by officers (he was absent on sick leave), the 26th Wisconsin arrived with the rest of the brigade at Gettysburg about 3 p. m. July 1 and was ordered at once to the front on the extreme right of the brigade

POS-A-11B-062.author: Col. William H. Jacobs
POS-A-11B-062.quote: At about 4 o'clock the regiment rallied on Cemetery Hill

place.printed: Cemetery Hill, behind the stone fence

POS-A-11B-062.activity: As stated to Colonel Jacobs by officers, at about 4 o'clock the regiment rallied on Cemetery Hill and was ordered behind the stone fence

POS-A-11C-003.author: Maj. Thomas W. Osbom
POS-A-11C-003.quote: A little after 10 a. m. the first battery (Dilger's) reached the town

place.printed: the front of and 300 yards beyond the town

POS-A-11C-003.activity: A little after 10 a. m. Dilger's battery (the first) reached the town and was ordered by Schurz to the front of and 300 yards beyond the town, where it engaged a rebel battery about 1,000 yards in front

POS-A-11C-005.author: Maj. Thomas W. Osbom
POS-A-11C-005.quote: About 11 a. m. Lieutenant Wilkeson reached the field

place.printed: about three-fourths of a mile from the town on the left of the York pike

POS-A-11C-005.activity: About 11 a. m. Lieutenant Wilkeson's Battery G reached the field and was ordered to report to Barlow, whose First Division was engaged about three-fourths of a mile from the town on the left of the York pike

POS-A-11C-010.author: Maj. Thomas W. Osbom
POS-A-11C-010.quote: About 3 p. m. they opened along our whole front with an unbroken line
POS-A-11C-010.activity: About 3 p. m. July 3 the enemy opened along the whole front with an unbroken line of artillery and heavily on the right flank

POS-A-11C-018.author: Lieut. William Wheeler
POS-A-11C-018.quote: At about 2 p. m. the rebel batteries opened along our front
POS-A-11C-018.activity: At about 2 p. m. the rebel batteries opened along the front and on the right flank; at about 5.30 p. m. the ammunition was exhausted and another battery was sent to relieve

POS-A-11C-021.author: Capt. Hubert DUger
POS-A-11C-021.quote: The battery arrived at Gettysburg at about 10 a. m. July 1

place.printed: Gettysburg; position "between the Taneytown and Baltimore road"

POS-A-11C-021.activity: The battery arrived at Gettysburg at about 10 a. m. July 1 attached to the division of Schurz, commanded by Brig. Gen. Schimmelfennig, who ordered it to a position (printed) between the Taneytown and Baltimore road

POS-A-11C-027.author: Lieut. Eugene A. Bancroft
POS-A-11C-027.quote: the battery reached the town at 11 a. m.

place.printed: the town; turning to the right, in rear of our lines of batteries, about 1 mile through some fields

POS-A-11C-027.activity: When about 2 miles out the order to trot was received; the battery reached the town at 11 a. m., passed through the village, turned right in rear of our lines of batteries and moved about 1 mile through fields

POS-A-11C-032.author: Lieut. Christopher F. Merkle
POS-A-11C-032.quote: about 1 mile or three-quarters northwest of the poor-house

place.printed: about 1 mile or three-quarters northwest of the poor-house

POS-A-11C-032.activity: Merkle's left section was assigned by Wilkeson a position about 3/4 to 1 mile northwest of the poor-house; retired when the infantry fell back and fired canister with the prolonge fixed at the end of the town

POS-A-1CA-016.author: Col. Charles S. Wainwright
POS-A-1CA-016.quote: no engagements occurred until about 4 p. m.

place.printed: Cemetery Hill batteries; enemy in a wheat-field at about 1,300 yards

POS-A-1CA-016.activity: No engagement on July 2 until about 4 p. m., when the enemy opened with twenty-pounders and Parrotts from a wheat-field at about 1,300 yards; replied with thirteen 3-inch guns for about an hour and a half

POS-A-1CA-022.author: Capt. James A. HaU
POS-A-1CA-022.quote: we opened fire in reply to the enemy's guns at 4.15 p. m.
POS-A-1CA-022.activity: July 2 opened fire in reply to the enemy's guns at 4.15 p. m., then relieved by a battery of the Reserve Artillery and sent to the rear to repair damages by order of Newton

POS-A-1D1-015.author: Maj. John Mansfield
POS-A-1D1-015.quote: approached Gettysburg from the Emmitsburg pike
POS-A-1D1-015.activity: 2nd Wisconsin, part of the First Brigade, had the right and approached Gettysburg from the Emmitsburg pike on the morning of July 1

POS-A-1D1-028.author: Col. WiUiam W. Eobinson
POS-A-1D1-028.quote: the Second Wisconsin leading, the Seventh next in column

when.printed: early on the morning of the 1st

place.printed: the road running from Emmitsburg to Gettysburg, about 5 miles from the latter place
place.direction_or_road: the road running from Emmitsburg to Gettysburg

POS-A-1D1-028.activity: 7th Wisconsin left its camp on the road running from Emmitsburg to Gettysburg, about 5 miles from Gettysburg, early on July 1 with the brigade, the Second Wisconsin leading, the Seventh next in column

POS-A-1D3-002.author: Brig. Gen. John C. Eobinson
POS-A-1D3-002.quote: by order of the majorgeneral commanding First Corps, in reserve, near the seminary
POS-A-1D3-002.activity: About 3 miles from Gettysburg the division was pushed forward and on arrival placed in reserve near the seminary by order of the corps commander

POS-A-1D3-012.author: Col. C!ol. Eichard Coulter
POS-A-1D3-012.quote: was massed on the west side and near the embankment of the railroad

place.printed: the west side and near the embankment of the railroad

POS-A-1D3-012.activity: About 11 a. m. the brigade was massed on the west side and near the embankment of the railroad

POS-A-1D3-049.author: Col. C:!ol. Gilbert G. Prey

POS-B-us-12c-1d-colgrove-05.activity: The reconnaissance went along the turnpike about 2 miles, thence by a cross-road to the Hanover road, and by the Hanover road to Gettysburg

POS-B-us-12c-25.author: Maj. Gen. Henry W. Halleck

POS-B-us-12c-2d-kane-19.activity: July 1: marched by the Baltimore turnpike to Two Taverns, and from there to within about 2 miles of Gettysburg

POS-B-us-2c-20.activity: Dispatch to the Sixth Corps (July 1, no hour printed): "the Second Corps is on the road between Taneytown and Gettysburg"; Twelfth Corps at Two Taverns, Fifth at Hanover, Third at Emmitsburg

POS-B-us-2c-3d-01.author: Brig. Gen. Alexander Hays

POS-B-us-2c-3d-01.activity: Division moving on the Taneytown road arrived within about a mile of the town and was assigned a position on a ridge nearly parallel with the road, facing west, with a stone wall just below the crest and half a mile of open ground in front

POS-B-us-3c-1d-13.author: Maj. Gen. David B. Bimey

POS-B-us-3c-25.author: Maj. Gen. Winfield S. Hancock

POS-B-us-3c-2d-carr-84pa-04.activity: July 2 to 4 picketing roads near the wagon parks; July 5 picketing roads and loading supply trains

place.printed: near the cemetery, on the left and rear of Gettysburg

POS-E-US-3C-2D-CARR-84PA-003.quote: to guard the supply train that was then located between Emmitsburg and Gettj'sburg

when.printed: On the morning of the 1st of July until the 6th of July

place.printed: the supply train then located between Emmitsburg and Gettysburg; with the train until relieved on the 6th of July, when it reported to Carr at Williamsport

POS-E-US-3C-2D-CARR-84PA-003.activity: Carr's letter, printed in the 84th Pennsylvania's address: on the morning of July 1 the regiment was detailed by an order from headquarters to guard the supply train then located between Emmitsburg and Gettysburg; it remained on duty with the train until relieved by another regiment on July 6, when it reported to Carr for duty at Williamsport. Carr adds that he would suggest the monument be erected near where his headquarters had been before the second day's engagement, near the Emmitsburg road directly in front of the Roger's House (a suggestion for the monument's site, not a statement that the regiment or its monument stood there).
